Output

Field branch: compact geometry/cost parameters, pose/gripper intent and control context.

Direct branch: five normalized 7D actions.

No ground-truth object pose, depth, contact or success signal enters the model.
Snapshot A · zero-shot obstacle Hybrid · decision before action index 201 (indices are zero-based).

Small structured output
Goal, up to four Gaussian repulsors, up to four blocked boxes and four unknown boxes.
All offsets are in meters along world axes, relative to the end-effector position when this Field was generated.
GPT does not emit 35,937 scalar distances.
The grid is centered once per Field refresh. Reuse does not expand known space.
35,937 grid vertices
Spacing along each grid axis
Span per axis: ±8 cm about the center

Coordinates: xijk = c + 0.005 · (i−16, j−16, k−16)

Validity: inside workspace AND outside predicted blocked / unknown regions.
Check graph edges and tracking chords against masks and closed boxes.

Unknown is not free.

Repulsors add soft cost; they do not create collision geometry.

5 mm resolution is a sampling choice, not 5 mm perception accuracy.
Distance is to a local goal region through predicted valid space—not distance to an obstacle surface.

26-neighbor graph
Reverse multi-source Dijkstra stores D and a successor toward the goal.

Units
Meters with no repulsors; weighted meters with repulsors.

Invalid / unreachable: +∞.
Goal endpoints: D = 0.
The current path objective is D. The compatibility potential U is still stored but does not drive Dijkstra.
Quantity
Meaning
Role / limitation
Legacy potential U
Weighted goal attraction + Gaussian bumps; dimensionless.
Expanded into GridField for compatibility. Current Dijkstra ignores U and attraction_weights.
Current distance D
Minimum weighted route length to the local goal region.
Computed locally on the valid graph. Exact for that finite augmented graph; not exact continuous geodesic distance.
Conventional SDF
Signed distance to the nearest obstacle surface.
Different quantity. This implementation does not reconstruct a surface-distance field from sensor geometry.
No claim of a full-scene metric, a Riemannian neural field, or a certified robot configuration-space planner.
A slice of the full 3D solve at the recorded start Y; the selected path lies in this XZ plane.
Snapshot A has no Gaussian repulsors: ρ = 1. The plot shows the model’s local masks and graph distances, not recovered physical obstacle geometry.
35,937 possible grid vertices are not 35,937 candidate trajectories.
Connect the measured start
Validate connections to enclosing grid corners; choose start-edge cost + D.
Follow stored successors
Extract a shortest graph route. Reuse cached D while the field and goal are unchanged.
Keep a short executable prefix
Merge only collinear edges. At most 10 segments, each ≤1 cm; at most 10 cm of geometric path.
Current tolerances: 2.5 mm goal-region radius + 2.5 mm tracking endpoint tolerance; outer arrival check = 5 mm and 0.05 rad. Invalid/out-of-map goals request a new observation.
Geometric segments, control ticks and model calls are different quantities.
Measured-pose path tracking

Project actual end-effector position onto the remaining path.

Choose a checked point up to 3 cm ahead.

Command position error, bounded to 5 cm norm. Shorten the reference if its chord crosses a predicted mask.
δx = bounded(x<sub>reference</sub> − x<sub>measured</sub>)
a = [δx / 0.05, δθ / 0.5, gripper]

Rotation error is capped at 0.15 rad.
Gripper: open −1, close +1, hold previous.
Actions go to the 20 Hz OSC controller.
Track for at most 10 control ticks per local plan, or replan earlier. A “10-step path” does not guarantee 10 cm of actual robot travel.
GPT selects phase and branch. Typical uses are shown below; phase names do not impose a fixed controller mapping.
Field branch

Approach / transport / alignment.
Local path tracking; initially up to 30 actions per model response.

Reliable visual progress may extend reuse to 60, 90, then 120 actions.
Direct branch

Grasp / release / contact recovery.
Five model-generated actions per response, executed unchanged.

Task termination can interrupt the final chunk.

Refresh early: measured arrival, invalid path/reference, boundary, low realized motion, lost tracking, or placement verification concerns. A phase label or “near_target” prediction is not proof of contact or success.
These mechanisms are conditional. Their existence in code does not mean they activated in a rollout.
Account for the held bowl

g = c + d − Rtarget RcurrentT r

c: Field center; d: desired bowl offset.
r: current bowl offset from the gripper.

Subtract the rotated grasp offset from the bowl goal. Assumes a visually estimated, rigid grasp.
Optional image-based XY correction

Track model-specified image points.
Fit a local 2×2 image Jacobian from measured XY motion.
Apply a validated correction ≤1 cm.

No depth reconstruction; masks and original grid center stay fixed.
Latest zero-shot run: all 13 Field outputs had no visual anchor; all 310 feedback records reported anchor unavailable. No local visual goal corrections or reuse extensions occurred.
Recorded actions 201–214, including local replanning; no simulated trajectory was substituted.
A 10-segment geometric prefix can be shorter than 10 cm. Tracking uses feedback to reduce error; commanded displacement is not equal to realized displacement.
Do not mix different success criteria or count failed-attempt durations as completed-task speedups.

The code retains the legacy potential representation alongside the new distance objective.
U(x) = √[Σ<sub>a</sub> α<sub>a</sub>((x<sub>a</sub>−g<sub>a</sub>)/ℓ)²] + Σ<sub>k</sub> β<sub>k</sub> exp(−‖x−r<sub>k</sub>‖² / (2σ<sub>k</sub>²))
ℓ = 0.08 m. U is dimensionless. Attraction weights α affect U, but not current Dijkstra edge weights.
Distance is goal-conditioned
D is a cost-to-go to one terminal region. It is not a scalar clearance to nearby obstacle surfaces.
Optimality has a precise scope
Reverse Dijkstra is exact on the constructed finite graph with endpoint-averaged density and valid terminal connections. It is not a continuous Eikonal/PDE solve.
